description: Offence keys printed with 4 digits until 2007 and 6 digits from 2008 (2200 becomes 220000). Mapped one to one in offence_map.csv.
evidence: Group legends of the PDF tables name the same offence groups in 2007 and 2008

description: The second PDF offence column changes from bodily harm (220000) to dangerous and serious bodily harm (222000). Separate keys, never linked (BUG-011, BUG-013).
evidence: PDF headers 2009 and 2010; 2013 publishes both: 220000 = 533,432 and 222000 = 127,833 nationally

description: Case counts are published from 2013 (Excel). For 2003 to 2012 counts are cases_derived = hz * population / 1e5 from rounded HZ (BUG-015).

HZ denominator based on Zensus 2011 (header: HZ nach Zensus 2011); PDF years use the population update of 1 January (BUG-026). The HZ of year t refers to the population of 31.12.(t - 1). Compare counts, or recompute rates on one census base with pksR::pks_rates(population = "corrected"), which uses the census-corrected population of the BBSR (column population_corrected).
HZ denominator based on Zensus 2022 (header: HZ nach Zensus 2022) (BUG-026). As for BRK-004, pksR::pks_rates(population = "corrected") puts all years on one census base.
890000 is published from 2015; for 2014 it is computed as ------ minus 725000 (suspects NA), as decided by the maintainer (question Q4 of the offence review).
evidence: Identity exact for cases, attempts and cleared in all 4,409 district rows 2015 to 2025

description: Three scopes in one key: 2014 to 2016 para. 177 Abs. 2 to 4 and 178 StGB; 2017 para. 177 Abs. 1 to 9 and 178 StGB after the reform of the sexual offences law; from 2018 only especially serious cases incl. resulting in death. A second break follows in 2018.

Labels add para. 244a StGB in 2016 and para. 244 Abs. 4 StGB from 2018. The cited paragraphs change, the offence described does not; the national series shows the known decline without a step at either year.
621020 and 621021 (until 2017) are replaced by 621100, 621110 and 621120 (paras. 113 to 115 StGB) from 2018. Not linked: assaults counted in 621020 move to the new 621120.
Fraud label adds paras. 265c to 265e StGB (new offences of 2017) in 2018.
Label adds killing on request (para. 216 StGB) in 2016; the step is larger than that offence alone suggests.
Summary key renamed from Computerkriminalitaet to Cybercrime in 2021, when 980100 leaves the table.

Some years are published on the previous year's boundary after mid-year reforms: 2008 on 2007, 2009 on 2008, 2011 on 2010, 2016 on 2015, 2021 on 2020. Harmonization starts from the published boundary (registry/sources.csv, boundary_year).
evidence: District sets per year match the BBSR crosswalk at that boundary (audit section 4)

description: Theft in/from motor vehicles (in/aus, until 2011) becomes theft of parts from and items out of motor vehicles (an/aus) in 2012. The BKA yearbook 2012 prints (-) instead of a change against 2011, i.e. not comparable.
evidence: Yearbook 2011: 242,563; yearbook 2012: 343,460 with (-); district sums 242,298 and 342,908

description: Cannabis Act (KCanG) in force from 1 April 2024: most cannabis possession offences no longer count as drug offences. The totals ------ and 890000 lose the same cases: their decline from 2023 to 2024 is smaller than the drop in 730000 alone.
The list of component keys disappears from the label in 2016 and the national count doubles; renamed Cybercrime im engeren Sinne in 2017 without a further step.
Unexplained step of 59 percent in 2016 with an unchanged label, at the same time as BRK-016.
